subject: Vanguard: ceiling amendment + special warranty language — exec sign-off required
messages:
From: Ethan Shaw <ethan.shaw@vanguard.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Karen Li <karen.li@vanguard.com>, procurement@vanguard.com
Date: Fri, 10 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SOW + Terms (follow-up)

Olga — thanks for the updated SOW. Our legal team ran a pass and there are two items they need leadership approval on before procurement can sign: (1) increase on the liability cap for security incidents from $2M to $7.5M (they want 3x ARR for the pilot); and (2) a short warranty carve-out for third-party model outputs for the period of the pilot.

We understand this is outside your standard playbook; can you flag whether Redwood can accept those two items or if an exec sign-off is required? We can accelerate if you can confirm today.

—Ethan
Ethan Shaw
Sr. Manager, Vendor Risk
Vanguard Asset Management

Attachment: Vanguard_SOW_comments.pdf (annotated)
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Shaw <ethan.shaw@vanguard.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Aug 2028 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SOW + Terms (follow-up)

Ethan — thanks for the quick review and the annotated SOW. I’ve looped in our sales and legal leads to evaluate. Short answer: the liability cap increase and the warranty carve-out are non-standard and will require approval from Deal Desk / CRO and legal leadership before we can commit. I’ll outline options below and propose next steps.

Options we can discuss with Vanguard:
- Accept a higher cap but keep it tied to an incident-based carve (e.g., single-incident limit vs aggregate) and exclude punitive damages.
- Offer a conditional pilot addendum with a limited timebox (90 days) and a separate uplifted cap while the pilot runs.
- Push back on warranty language by confirming we will operate models in a best-effort manner and provide indemnity only for Redwood-managed infrastructure issues.

Next steps: I’ll get input from Legal (Laura) on acceptable language and Ben (sales lead) on commercial flexibility. If needed, we’ll escalate to Marissa for exec sign-off on cap variance. I’ll be back with options by Monday.

Thanks,
Olga
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com
Attachment: Vanguard_redlines_OLGA_comments.docx
From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 13 Aug 2028 08:23:00 -0700
Subject: RE: SOW + Terms (follow-up)

Olga / Ben — reviewed Vanguard’s redlines. Key legal notes: 
1) Liability cap: moving to $7.5M is material. We can consider a timeboxed pilot cap at that level but only if: (a) it is expressly limited to the pilot scope, (b) Vanguard accepts a single-incident aggregate (not separate per-customer claims), and (c) we get a commercial uplift (pro-rated fee uplift or one-time credit to cover incremental risk).
2) Indemnity: they added broader indemnities for model outputs. We should limit indemnity to claims arising from Redwood’s breach of the agreement or Redwood-managed infrastructure, and exclude claims based on Customer-provided data / instructions.
3) Warranty: propose a mutual limited warranty — Redwood warrants infrastructure availability and correct delivery of API outputs, but disclaims warranty for model decision correctness; add a cooperation clause for reproducing issues.

Given (1)-(3) it’s a non-standard terms escalation. Marissa (CRO) will need to sign off on the elevated cap or approve the commercial uplift. Please schedule a short call if Vanguard wants to move forward quickly.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
General Counsel (commercial contracts)
Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 14 Aug 2028 09:01:00 -0700
Subject: RE: SOW + Terms (follow-up)

Team — quick commercial note: Vanguard is strategic with potential for enterprise expansion across three lines if pilot goes well (est. $1.2M ARR in year 1). I recommend we consider the timeboxed cap approach and ask for a 15% pilot fee uplift or a one-time risk surcharge of $75k to offset the elevated exposure. If Marissa signs, we can accept the pilot cap and proceed to DocuSign.

Marissa — can you confirm approval authority for a one-time surcharge and cap variance? If you want, I can draft the commercial note for your signoff.

Thanks,
Ben
VP, Sales Operations
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, olga.petrov@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 14 Aug 2028 11:17:00 -0700
Subject: RE: SOW + Terms (follow-up)

Ben / Olga / Laura — I’ve read the summary. Given Vanguard’s strategic potential and the clear scope limitation to a 90-day pilot, I’m prepared to approve the elevated pilot cap to $7.5M with the following conditions:
1) The cap is explicitly limited to the pilot period and a pilot SOW exhibit;
2) We add the indemnity carve (Redwood only indemnifies breaches of the agreement or infrastructure);
3) Vanguard signs the 15% pilot fee uplift (or $75k one-time surcharge) — finance to confirm final accounting treatment;
4) Legal to prepare the specific language and the pilot exhibit;

I approve this as an exception. Olga, get DocuSign-ready SOW and route to Finance for the surcharge paperwork. Laura, please draft the exhibit and redline the warranty language. I’ll be available for a quick sign-off after you circulate.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Chief Revenue Officer, Redwood Inference

If Vanguard is good with that approach I’ll push the SOW to DocuSign today. SOW / exhibit and a short summary will be attached for your review.

Thanks for moving quickly — Olga
